title: The heads of the biggest AI labs want to agree among themselves on when everyone should slow down. @TheEconomist's piece on that push ends with Covenant-72B, the model we finished training in March on GPUs contributed over the internet, as a reason such agreements may be hard to enforce. text: Anthropic (@AnthropicAI) We’ve trained Claude to flag potential misuse in conversations, a technique we call self-assessment. Right after it responds, Claude gives a preliminary safety assessment of the conversation. Since we began using self-assessment in June, it has surfaced misuse that our other safeguards weren’t designed to catch. Because Claude has already read the conversation, self-assessment is very efficient. And unlike classifiers, which target a discrete set of harms, it draws on Claude’s own judgment, so it gets more accurate as our models improve. Read more on our new Safeguards

title: RT by @rob_svrn: A credibly neutral network state with its own economy and currency being essential to the proliferation of truly open intelligence is a profound concept. After much study I’ve concluded the same and think that it’s an inevitability. I would **highly** recommend listening to this weeks novelty search where @const_reborn went more in depth on this. He also highlighted what’s coming down the pike next week with updates to Bittensor’s wallet infrastructure in light of the recent AI advancements in mathematics. Bittensor wallets will be able to hide the signing key behind a hash and swap in a new one after every transaction, with post-quantum signatures layered on top, so an elliptic-curve break alone can’t drain them.
